What affects the cost of AI consulting?

What affects the cost of AI consulting and automation? Compare scope, integrations, ongoing fees and a useful first pilot before requesting a quote.

By Ben Young · Business owner & AI consultant
Updated 16 November 2026

On this page
  • Separate the first project from the ongoing costs
  • The things that change the scope
  • Estimate the value using your own numbers
  • What to bring to a scoping conversation
  • Choose a first project that can prove its value

The useful question is what a specific improvement will cost to build and run. “AI for my business” can mean a short discovery exercise, one automation or a custom operational app. Those are different projects, so a meaningful quote starts with a defined task and outcome.

Separate the first project from the ongoing costs

A proposal should make clear what is included in discovery, development, testing and rollout. It should also explain what happens after launch. Hosting, AI usage, automation subscriptions, maintenance and support may continue even if some existing software subscriptions disappear.

I scope work around your actual systems and workflow rather than quoting an invented standard package. We agree the work, cost and success criteria before starting.

The things that change the scope

  • Number of systems. One handover is different from coordinating several apps that each store part of a job.
  • Access to the data. Supported APIs and clean exports are easier to work with than incomplete records or restricted access.
  • Consequences of an error. A draft report needs different checks from an action that updates operational records.
  • Migration. Historical jobs, attachments, permissions and a cutover plan add work beyond the new features.
  • Support expectations. Monitoring, response arrangements and future changes need to be defined.

Estimate the value using your own numbers

Count how often a task happens, the time it takes now and the time that will still be needed to review the output. Multiply the difference by your own cost of staff time. Keep subscription changes separate so you don’t count the same benefit twice.

For example, a hypothetical task done 30 times a week that saves six minutes each time releases three hours a week. That is an illustration of the calculation, not a forecast. Whether those hours become lower costs, extra capacity or a shorter working day depends on the business.

A useful comparison: annual cost of the new setup = ongoing software and usage fees + hosting + maintenance and support + the build cost spread over the period you choose. Compare that with the costs and workarounds of the current setup.

What to bring to a scoping conversation

  1. One task you want to improve, from its trigger to its finished output.
  2. The names and plans of the systems involved.
  3. A representative example with private information removed.
  4. How often the task happens and roughly how long it takes.
  5. The people who will use the result and the checks they need.

Choose a first project that can prove its value

A single systems integration or AI-assisted workflow may answer the question before you commit to a larger app. Measure it against the old process, including the time spent checking and correcting results.

My own business removed over $80,000 in annual subscriptions after replacing our SaaS tools with one in-house app. That number is subscription spend removed, not net savings after building and running the app. Read the full context, or tell me about the task you want to improve.
